content:
Partition \(\{1,2,\dots,150\}\) into 50 blocks:
\[
\{1,2,3\},\{4,5,6\},\dots,\{148,149,150\}.
\]
If a subset has no three consecutive integers, it can contain at most 2 marbles from each block. Thus such a subset has size at most
\[
50\cdot 2=100.
\]
This bound is attainable by choosing the first two numbers from each block:
\[
1,2,4,5,7,8,\dots,148,149,
\]
which has 100 elements and no three consecutive integers. Therefore the maximum size without three consecutive integers is 100, so the smallest guaranteed size is
\[
100+1=101.
\]
\[
\boxed{101}
\]
